items.title: The Falklands War
items.line: Argentina invaded the Falklands on 2 April 1982 and surrendered on 14 June after 74 days. 255 British servicemen died, and the win carried Thatcher to a bigger majority the next year.

items.title: ZX Spectrum
items.line: Sinclair's rubber-keyed home computer went on sale on 23 April 1982, built in Dundee by Timex and loading games off cassette. It sold over five million.

items.title: Blade Runner
items.line: Ridley Scott's film opened in 1,290 US cinemas on 25 June 1982 and underperformed, with a Vangelis synth score nominated for a BAFTA. Scott shot Roxy Music's 'Avalon' video the same year.

items.title: Mary Rose raised
items.line: Henry VIII's warship, which saw her last action in 1545, was raised on 11 October 1982 by the Mary Rose Trust while Prince Charles watched from a boat.

items.title: Compact disc
items.line: The compact disc, co-developed by Philips and Sony and sized to hold 74 minutes of stereo audio, first went on sale in Japan in October 1982.

items.title: Channel 4 launches
items.line: Britain's fourth channel began on 2 November 1982 from Scala House in London, joining BBC1, BBC2 and ITV. It was paid for by advertising, not the licence fee.

items.title: The Tube
items.line: Channel 4's live music show started on 5 November 1982, made by Tyne Tees in Newcastle and hosted by Jools Holland and Paula Yates. It ran to 121 episodes by 1987.

items.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
items.line: Spielberg's E.T. opened in the US on 11 June 1982 on a $10.5 million budget. In 1983 it passed Star Wars as the highest-grossing film ever and held the record until Jurassic Park in 1993.

items.title: Commodore 64
items.line: Commodore showed the C64 at CES in Las Vegas in January 1982 and started selling it in August at $595. Guinness lists it as the best-selling desktop computer model of all time.

items.title: Cheers
items.line: Cheers premiered on NBC on 30 September 1982 and ranked 74th in its first season. It survived to run 275 episodes and win 28 Primetime Emmys.

items.title: Italy win the World Cup
items.line: Italy beat West Germany 3-1 at the Santiago Bernabéu in Madrid on 11 July 1982, with goals from Paolo Rossi, Marco Tardelli and Alessandro Altobelli in front of 90,089.
